html:
The Xingu Indigenous Park is a large protected territory on the upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, Brazil, created in 1961 as the country's first big Indigenous territory. More than a dozen peoples live there.

The Villas-Bôas brothers, Orlando, Cláudio and Leonardo, met the upper Xingu peoples on a government expedition in the 1940s and campaigned for years, with the anthropologist Darcy Ribeiro, to protect their land from ranchers.

The upper Xingu peoples, such as the Kamaiurá and Kalapalo, speak languages of several unrelated families yet share one way of life: round villages of large thatched houses around a plaza, manioc and fish, and shared rites such as the Kuarup for the dead. Others were moved in from outside as roads and ranches advanced, among them the Kayabí, the Ikpeng and the Panará, while the Kĩsêdjê and part of the Yudjá already lived on the river.

Today soy fields and cattle pasture press on every side, and satellite pictures show the park as a green island in cleared land.
sum: The Xingu Indigenous Park is a large protected territory on the upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, Brazil, created in 1961 as the country's first big Indigenous territory. More than a dozen peoples live there.
